records.Entity / project type: Early Ordinals marketplace using native and/or Emblem Vault pathways
records.Concise description: Historically important early Ordinals venue associated with Emblem Vault-based Ethereum trading and early PSBT market development.
records.Deeper researched summary: Ordinals Market was a material early Ordinals venue during the first months of 2023. Galaxy Research identifies Ordinals Market, Ordinals Wallet and Ordswap as the venues that dominated early trading from February through April 2023. Gamma's historical marketplace guide describes Ordinals Market as Ethereum-infrastructure based, using vaults that issue an Ethereum representation of the Ordinal, while Coinbase Institutional reported on March 31, 2023 that ordinals.market was among venues adopting PSBTs for trust-minimized inscription trading. Those sources imply multiple trading pathways or a product transition that cannot be reconstructed confidently from current first-party documentation. The registry preserves that ambiguity rather than falsely calling the entire venue either purely native Bitcoin or purely wrapped Ethereum.
Creators / founders: Ordinals Market team; reliable founder attribution was not established from reviewed sources
records.Launch / history: Prominent in the February–March 2023 emergence of Ordinals markets. By later 2023 the market had consolidated around other venues; meaningful current operation was not verified in this research pass.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin marketplac: Ordinals Market captures the transitional moment when early Bitcoin inscription liquidity used both Bitcoin PSBT techniques and cross-chain vault representations before native Bitcoin marketplaces matured.

Corroborating sources.label: Galaxy Research — Bitcoin Inscriptions & Ordinals: A Maturing Ecosystem

records.Verification basis: Contemporary independent/institutional research and a competing marketplace's historical explainer establish early significance but do not fully resolve whether the venue used multiple settlement paths over time.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do NOT publish an unqualified custody or settlement description. Contemporary sources differ: Crypto.com emphasizes Emblem Vault/Ethereum trading, while Coinbase includes ordinals.market among PSBT venues. Exact product-transition chronology remains unresolved. Current lifecycle is treated as HISTORICAL because no meaningful 2026 operation was verified.

records.Entity / project type: Early Ordinals marketplace and inscription service
records.Concise description: Early 2023 trust-minimized Ordinals marketplace using PSBTs that later ceased safe operation after losing control of its domain.
records.Deeper researched summary: Ordswap launched in February 2023 as one of the first dedicated Ordinals marketplaces and inscription services. Contemporary sources describe PSBT-based trust-minimized trading. In October 2023 the Ordswap team warned users not to connect to its domain after losing control of it; the site reportedly displayed a phishing/drainer flow and the team published a recovery route for some users. No active successor marketplace was verified. Because the project ceased rather than simply completing a planned product phase, MSC classifies it INACTIVE while preserving its historical significance.
records.Launch / history: Launched February 2023. Became an early PSBT marketplace and inscription service. Lost control of its domain in October 2023; safe continued marketplace operation was not verified afterward.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin marketplac: Ordswap was part of the first generation that replaced Discord/OTC Ordinals trading with PSBT-based marketplace flows and helped establish the transaction pattern later adopted more broadly.

Corroborating sources.label: Cointelegraph — domain loss and recovery warning

records.Verification basis: Contemporary independent research supports launch/mechanics; security reporting and reproduced team warnings support cessation. The compromised historical domain is intentionally not linked.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not restore or publish the old Ordswap domain as an official link without a fresh security verification. Exact post-incident shutdown chronology is not fully documented in stable first-party sources, so 'INACTIVE' is based on no verified successor/current operation plus the documented domain loss.

records.Concise description: Open-source zero-fee early Ordinals marketplace that demonstrated seller-created PSBT offers and buyer-completed Bitcoin settlement.
records.Deeper researched summary: OpenOrdex is one of the clearest technical artifacts from the first Ordinals marketplace wave. Its public GitHub repository describes an open-source, zero-fee, 'trustless Bitcoin NFT marketplace' where the seller creates a PSBT specifying price and the buyer signs and broadcasts the completed transaction. Galaxy highlighted it in March 2023 as a notable fully open-source PSBT marketplace. The repository remains public and unarchived, but its latest observed commits are from August 2023; no meaningful current consumer marketplace operation was verified. MSC therefore treats it as a historical protocol/product artifact, not ACTIVE merely because GitHub is reachable.
records.Launch / history: Active during the first 2023 Ordinals marketplace wave. Public repository's most recent observed commits are August 2023; no current operating marketplace was verified in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin marketplac: OpenOrdex is historically important because its source code and simple seller-PSBT/buyer-completion model made the early trust-minimized Ordinals marketplace pattern legible and reproducible.
Important technical or cultural characte: zero marketplace fee in original README
records.Verification basis: Official source code/README establishes mechanics; repository history and absence of verified live operation control lifecycle.
Research notes / uncertainties: Repository reachability is not evidence of current marketplace operation. HISTORICAL rather than INACTIVE because the open-source artifact persists and no explicit abandonment/shutdown statement was found. Lifecycle could be revisited if a maintained deployment is verified.

records.Entity / project type: Bitcoin-native AMM/DEX infrastructure for Runes and BRC-20
records.Concise description: Bitcoin-native token AMM with both custodial CPMM pools and self-custodial Nexus liquidity pools, supporting Runes and BRC-20.
records.Deeper researched summary: DotSwap is a modular Bitcoin DEX for BTC, Runes and BRC-20. Its architecture is especially important for custody precision: first-party docs label DotSwap LP Pools as custodial constant-product pools whose funds are managed through a Multi-layer Multi-signature Matrix using MPC/native multisig, while Nexus LP Pools are self-custodial concentrated-liquidity pools operated by LP nodes and coordinated through threshold multisig. This mixed architecture means DotSwap cannot be summarized accurately with one blanket custody adjective. Satflow currently routes external purchase construction to DotSwap, and Xverse identifies it among Rune swap providers.
Creators / founders: DotSwap team; individual founders were not established from reviewed first-party sources
records.Launch / history: Active by the Runes era and continues to expose current Bitcoin-native liquidity/trading architecture and integrations in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin marketplac: DotSwap is one of the strongest examples of Bitcoin fungible-token liquidity moving from simple PSBT order books toward AMM infrastructure while retaining Bitcoin UTXO/transaction constraints.

Corroborating sources.label: Xverse — How to Swap Runes using Xverse Wallet

records.Verification basis: First-party architecture is controlling for custody/pool design; current integrations corroborate active ecosystem use.
Research notes / uncertainties: Never describe DotSwap simply as 'non-custodial.' The platform documents two pool models with different custody properties. Specific pool fees are configurable/time-sensitive and should be checked before publication.
